claims.statement: In late June 1875 there was talk of a match between Tom Allen and Ned O'Baldwin, and for three months efforts to arrange a meeting were made.
claims.excerpt: alk ofa match to be made between O’Baldwin and Allen

claims.statement: The paper said that had Ned O'Baldwin lived, a contest with Tom Allen would certainly have taken place the next spring.
claims.excerpt: ned O’ Baldwin lived, a contest would certainty have taken place next. spring

claims.statement: In an exhibition for the Chicago fire sufferers in St. Louis, Tom Allen stopped Ned O'Baldwin in a glove bout, showing clear superiority.
claims.excerpt: Tom ‘‘stopped’’ hia in a manner which declared evident superiority

claims.statement: Immediately after that exhibition, Jack Leoney offered $5,000 to back Tom Allen in a match.
claims.excerpt: immediately on the close of the exhibition, Jack Leoney offered to plank down $5,000 to back

claims.statement: A Globe-Democrat reporter called on Tom Allen at his saloon on Washington avenue in St. Louis on September 29, 1875.
claims.excerpt: rom yesterday afternoon, at his saloon

notes: 'rom' (printed) is probably Tom, so the saloon claim is medium. The 1871 glove bout was a charity exhibition, so it is an exhibition, not a fight. O'Baldwin's death and career are not about Allen and are left out.
